Diagnosis:
CAUSE: Node `sre-lab-worker2` (cluster-scoped, context kind-sre-lab) is NotReady because its kubelet stopped posting node status, so the API server cannot reach the kubelet on 172.20.0.5:10250.

EVIDENCE:
1. `kubectl --context kind-sre-lab get node sre-lab-worker2 -o jsonpath=...conditions`: Ready, MemoryPressure, DiskPressure and PIDPressure are all `Unknown` with reason `NodeStatusUnknown` and message "Kubelet stopped posting node status."
2. `kubectl --context kind-sre-lab logs -n kube-system kube-proxy-74ls5 --tail=5`: exit code 1, `dial tcp 172.20.0.5:10250: connect: connection refused`.
3. diag-k8s `kubectl --context kind-sre-lab describe node sre-lab-worker2`: node carries taints `node.kubernetes.io/unreachable` (NoExecute and NoSchedule); last condition heartbeat 01:30:18.
4. diag-k8s `kubectl --context kind-sre-lab get events -A --sort-by=.lastTimestamp`: `Normal NodeNotReady node/sre-lab-worker2` (2 occurrences over 110m), then `Warning NodeNotReady` on kube-system kindnet and kube-proxy pods and on the cert-manager pods.
5. diag-k8s `kubectl --context kind-sre-lab get nodes -o wide`: `sre-lab-worker2 NotReady` at 172.20.0.5, while the control plane and `sre-lab-worker` are Ready.

FIX (not applied): Restart the kubelet on the sre-lab-worker2 node (the kind node container), then check its kubelet journal to find why it stopped posting status.

Fact.Name: cause
Fact.Value: the kubelet stopped: `Kubelet stopped posting node status` (every condition `Unknown`), not memory, disk or PID pressure

Fact.Name: side effect
Fact.Value: taint `node.kubernetes.io/unreachable`; its pods are marked not ready

Fact.Name: fix (not applied)
Fact.Value: restart the kubelet on the host (`systemctl start kubelet`); cordon the node meanwhile
